ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and continuously thereafter, screen all direct and indirect owners, UBOs, managers, directors, authorized representatives, major counterparties, and payment beneficiaries against United Nations Security Council lists, European Union consolidated sanctions lists, French national sanctions measures, OFAC lists where relevant to U.S. nexus or USD clearing, and reputable PEP databases. Apply enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, adverse-media review, and enhanced transaction monitoring for PEPs. Do not treat absence from an OFAC list as a substitute for EU, French, or UN screening. A proprietary HFT business must also implement market-abuse surveillance under Regulation (EU) No. 596/2014 and preserve algorithmic trading records.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI: https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; registration data are transmitted to the Registre national des entreprises (RNE).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be sufficiently distinctive and must not create confusion with an existing protected name, trademark, trade name, or corporate name. A SARL name must include the designation Société à responsabilité limitée or SARL and the stated capital. French characters and Latin script are accepted. A foreign-language name may be used if it is not misleading and complies with public-order, consumer-protection, trademark, and regulated-activity rules. No general statutory transliteration requirement applies, but the name must be entered in a form accepted by the Guichet unique and official registers.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any name implying authorization as a regulated financial institution without the required approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general statutory company-name reservation procedure or statutory 30-day reservation period. Conduct an INPI/RNE availability search, trademark search through INPI and EUIPO, domain-name search, and conflict review before filing. If the Guichet unique, registry, or competent authority rejects the name, obtain the electronic rejection notice, correct the name or supporting evidence, and resubmit through the Guichet unique within the applicable correction period. A formal administrative challenge may be filed with the competent authority and, where legally available, before the competent administrative court within the deadline stated in the rejection notice. A refusal based on trademark infringement, misleading financial terminology, or regulated-activity implication should normally be resolved by changing the name or obtaining the relevant authorization rather than by appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French company must have a registered office in France under Commercial Code Articles L.123-11 and following. A domiciliation company may be used only if it is authorized under the applicable domiciliation rules and a written domiciliation agreement is maintained. A virtual office is generally insufficient for a proprietary high-frequency algorithmic trading business that requires regulated investment-firm authorization, effective management, secure systems, compliance personnel, books and records, and demonstrable operational capacity. The registered office should not be treated as a substitute for regulatory substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official percentage is published. The risk is low for a dormant ordinary SARL but medium to high for a financial-sector applicant and high where the entity seeks investment-firm authorization, direct market access, algorithmic trading approval, or maintains only a mailbox address. AMF, ACPR, tax, customs, labor, and judicial authorities may conduct document requests or on-site inspections without a predictable public probability.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), notably Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 governing SARL formation, capital, management and share transfers; L.210-1 to L.210-10 on general company provisions; Civil Code Article 1835 et seq. for statutory formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce — commercial court registry, administered through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INFOGREFFE.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 (standard registration/formation form) filed together with the signed Statuts of the SARL through the Guichet Unique electronic portal, followed by issuance of the Kbis extraction.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for a SARL; the share capital is freely fixed in the Statuts. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed and at least one-fifth of the nominal value of each share must be paid up on formation. The paid-up cash capital must be deposited into a blocked escrow account with a bank or notary and remains blocked until the Kbis is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The shareholders unanimously subscribe the entire share capital of [Company Name] SARL, representing [€X] fully allocated to [Shareholders]. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [Address], France, and all corporate records are maintained there. RESOLVED: [Name] is appointed Gérant (General Manager) for an indefinite term, with sole authority to manage, represent the Company, and operate the registered account with [Bank]. RESOLVED: The Company shall immediately file the incorporation dossier with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, publish the required legal notice, and implement the Authorisation of the investment firm licence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the Articles of Association and capital subscription documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders; notary optional but required for real-property contributions or for the deposit of cash contributions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding shareholders must sign the Statuts in one or multiple originals, specifying the SARL legal form, corporate name, registered office address, object clause, share capital breakdown, duration, and management rules. If non-cash contributions are made, a notary must establish their valuation. The cash subscription declaration and contribution certificates must be aligned with the final share capital schedule.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts in French (two originals if no notary)
Subscription and contribution declaration for each founder
Notarised deed of valuation for any apports en nature (if applicable)
Power of attorney if one shareholder represents another
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the Statuts for missing or contradictory clauses, the shareholders must adopt a corrective resolution and re-sign an amended version before resubmission. Any valuation issue in non-cash contributions is cured by appointing a court-approved commissaire aux apports.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the blocked capital deposit account and pay up the share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; alternatively the deposit may be made with a notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each cash shareholder transfers the full subscribed amount to a temporary blocked account opened in the future company's name. The bank or notary must issue a certificate of deposit (attestation de blocage) expressly identifying the depositor, the Bearer of the deposits, and the total amount. For non-cash contributions, the notary's valuation inventory is attached. The release of funds occurs only upon presentation of the Kbis.
required_dossiers: Draft Statuts
Identity document of each cash subscriber
Kbis or certificate of existence for any corporate shareholder
Bank payment instruction evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the deposit due to incomplete corporate structure, the founders may select another authorized bank and transfer immediately. Should the valuation of a contribution be challenged, the corporate object must be amended or the in-kind contribution converted into cash payment-up.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the legal notice of incorporation in a journal d'annonces légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A formally authorized Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) selected from the prefecture's list for the locality of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The draft legal notice must be submitted to the JAL with the company name, corporate form, share capital, registered office address, object, duration, and the name of the Gérant. The notice is published in accordance with the Code de commerce requirements. Proof of publication, being the attestation de parution, must be obtained in the name of the company.
required_dossiers: Draft legal notice text
Final or signed Statuts
Attestation of blocked capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the newspaper refuses publication because of inconsistent data, the founders must amend and sign a corrected version of the Statuts and resubmit the notice. A publication certificate is procurable promptly after the corrected notice is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the incorporation application through the Guichet Unique / INFOGREFFE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, electronically transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office's territorial jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founders or their legal counsel must prepare the electronic M0 file and upload the signed Statuts, proof of capital deposit, legal notice publication proof, registered-office address proof, and the beneficial-owner declaration. The Greffe verifies legal completeness, capacity of subscribers, and compliance of the object clause. Fees are settled electronically by card or bank transfer at submission.
required_dossiers: Formulaire M0 completed online
Signed Statuts (scanned PDF)
Attestation de blocage de fonds
Attestation de parution de l'avis de constitution
Proof of address for the registered office (lease, title deed or accommodation agreement)
Declaration of beneficial owner (DBO form)
Minute or deed of appointment for company officials
Anti-money laundering information and due diligence of each shareholder, if triggered by law
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a notice of irregularity or requests rectification, the applicant must respond within the regulatory time limit, typically 15 days, by submitting the missing attestations or amending the statutory provisions. Repeated refusal may be cured by judicial referral to the registry supervisor.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive the Kbis extract and complete RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce issuing the official Kbis (extract of the Trade and Companies Register).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, the Greffe issues the Kbis confirming that the SARL is legally formed and duly registered. The Kbis is transmitted electronically to the Gérant and becomes the company's identity document for opening bank accounts, obtaining relevant financial licences, and applying for the ACPR/AMF approval.
required_dossiers: No further form is required; the Kbis is issued based on the submitted application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is not received within the indicative time, the applicant may log into the Guichet Unique to verify pending conditions or contact the Greffe's front desk. Any unpaid registry charges are remedied immediately by card payment or by receiving a reissuance receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration declarations and occupational safety arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF; direction départementale de l'emploi (DREETS or Direccte territorial offices housed in DREETS in some regions); tax office of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Gérant must ensure the company's SIREN/SIRET number is official, register employees with URSSAF, and, where applicable, post the first bulletin de déclaration sociale for staff. The company must also file with the tax office for corporate income tax, VAT, and the annual statement of existence. All premises must comply with health and safety requirements before operational activity begins.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
BAPS/DSN declaration for any initial employee
Registered office lease and fire-safety pre-diagnosis
Gérant's ID and appointment deed for acceptance
Registration of compliance officer and local physical location, if required by the financial licensing dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the employment or tax registration is queried, the company must reconcile the SIRET number with the Kbis and re-submit missing forms or proof of address to URSSAF within the statutory deadline. For safety defects, an architect or the local control commission can issue a remedial certificate for petty technical non-compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), acting jointly with the Autorité des Marchés Financiers (AMF) for investment services and market activities under the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) transposing MiFID II.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agrément en qualité de prestataire de services d'investissement (Investment Services Provider approval) covering algorithmic and high-frequency trading activity, supplemented by notification to AMF of the market-making arrangement, if applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique – Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) for installations, declared under the ICPE regime if a physical infrastructure is installed in the head office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / no full EIA due to the financial services scope. Algorithmic trading does not operate a manufacturing plant or a polluting industrial installation, so no formal environmental impact assessment is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable, because no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous process discharge is generated. Electronic equipment, servers, and IT hardware must comply with the waste electrical and electronic equipment framework under Directive 2012/19/EU and French Articles R.543-172 et seq. of the Environmental Code for disposal, reuse, and recycling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the registered office and any hosting premises, obtain a fire safety certificate from the local fire safety commission (attestation de sécurité incendie) for tertiary-use buildings, perform a structural load assessment if dedicated data racks are installed, and register the workplace with the occupational health service of the DREETS. No explosive or environmental risk clearance is required for a pure financial trading office, but the company must maintain a fire alarm and escape plan review before first employees occupy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — impots.gouv.fr; VAT and customs ancillary competence exercised by Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) — douane.gouv.fr; centralised incorporation and tax registration portal: Guichet Unique / formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL obtains its statutory tax identity ex lege upon corporate formation. The constitutional legal representative files the incorporation dossier (form MO-4) with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the online Guichet Unique. The registre then assigns the SIREN (9-digit statutory identifier), the SIRET (establishment identifier), and the code APE/NAF corresponding to ISIC 6499. The DGFiP automatically allocates the TVA intracommunautaire number (FR + 11 digits) upon verification of the incorporation file, normally within four to eleven business days. For a non-resident entity not yet possessing a French establishment, the DGFiP requires an individual application on the Cerfa no. 15768 form or the standard VAT registration application, supported by a certificate of fiscal domicile, the foreign company deed, and proof of the responsible fiscal representative when the non-resident has no permanent representative in France. Registration must be completed before any taxable supply, intra-Community acquisition, or import is made.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A standard SARL is irrebuttably within the scope of French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at the entity level under Article 206(1) of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI). Statutory elections available include: (i) the Article 239 bis AA CGI option for newly created SMEs to be taxed as a transparent partnership (régime fiscal des sociétés de personnes) for the first five fiscal years or until the corporation meets the SME thresholds, requiring unanimous shareholder consent and prompt filing; (ii) for an EURL (single-member SARL), the default pass-through taxation under Article 1655 bis CGI unless an irrevocable IS election is made; (iii) the groupe fiscal d'intégration election under Article 223 A CGI allowing a French parent to consolidate wholly- or 95%-owned French subsidiaries for IS purposes; and (iv) no check-the-box regime exists in French law, but hybrid mismatch elections may arise through the design of the foreign parent's entity characterisation; the French entity is nevertheless always treated as corporation-taxable absent the 239 bis AA election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The DGFiP 'franchise en base de TVA' exemption under Article 293 B CGI applies only to small businesses with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 85,000 for sales of goods and EUR 37,500 for services. This threshold is de facto unavailable for the present algorithmic high-frequency trading vehicle because principal trading is not a taxable supply and any fee-based financial services are VAT exempt under Article 261 C(1) CGI, while cross-border B2B financial services fall under the reverse charge irrespective of turnover. No general economic threshold triggers compulsory VAT registration for a SARL engaged in financial or FX trading; registration is mandatory from the first euro of taxable activity, and the franchise exemption cannot be invoked by a deliberately structured HFT entity. Intra-Community acquisition of goods is registrable regardless of value, and the OSS/IOSS regimes are inapplicable to exempt financial services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France enforces a phased e-invoicing mandate (facturation électronique) from 1 September 2026 for all VAT-registered businesses: acceptance of electronic invoices becomes compulsory for all B2B transactions, and structured electronic invoices must be transmitted through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or an accredited Plateforme de Dématerialisation Partenaire (PDP). From 2024-2025, large enterprises are subject to earlier e-reporting stages. Real-time fiscal clearance is not a French VAT concept; the system relies on continuous transmission of invoice data and e-reporting of transaction summaries. For crypto-asset and algorithmic trading services, the invoice must contain a specific exemption reference (e.g. Article 261 C CGI) and the reverse-charge indication for cross-border B2B supplies. Payment data, order-routing logs, and attestations from the financial services regulator must be retained as part of the pièces justificatives to support e-reporting accuracy. No digital stamping or crypto-graphic fiscal capping applies to French invoices, but the mandatory QR-code Datamatrix was never adopted; instead the PPF/PDP transmission data is the legally probative record.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, exports outside the European Union are zero-rated under Article 262 CGI provided the goods physically leave the EU customs territory within thirty days of the transfer of power of disposal and the exporter retains the harmonised proof of exit. For services, the zero-rating or test figure 'hors champ' is reached where the place of supply is outside France under Articles 259, 259 A and 259 B CGI; a French SARL supplying financial or market-making services to a non-resident taxable person applies the reverse charge and does not charge French VAT, which is equivalent to zero-rating. Because the present ISIC 6499 model operates proprietary ultra-low-latency algorithmic market making, no fee-bearing supply may exist; own-account trading falls outside the scope of VAT and no VAT claim or refund arises. If the SARL provides fee-based algorithmic execution, liquidity-provider services, or brokerage to non-EU banks or investment firms, zero-rating eligibility requires proof that (i) the recipient is a taxable person established in a third state, (ii) the service does not benefit a French or EU fixed establishment, and (iii) the consideration is computed as a fee or spread, not as a capital gain. The DGFiP applies the 'effective use and enjoyment' rule to determine the place of supply for B2B services supplied to third-country recipients.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane / EAD) lodged electronically on the DELTA system under the Union Customs Code, reflecting the proper goods nomenclature and the UE exit regime
Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), or CMR consignment note proving physical departure from French customs territory to a non-EU destination
Proof of exit with the customs office stamp or the electronic Export Accompanying Document (EAD) and the certificate of exit from the border office
Commercial invoice and, where applicable, the service contract or order-routing confirmation identifying the non-EU recipient and the VAT exemption or reverse-charge clause
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank settlement vouchers evidencing payment receipt from the foreign counterparty in convertible currency and traceability of the funds within 180 days

For algorithm-as-a-service and FX market-making: counterparty entity documentation (LEI code, tax residence certificate, place of effective management evidence) proving the recipient's third-country establishment
Trade reconstruction file (time-stamped order audit trail) demonstrating that the supplied service, if any, is distinct from proprietary gains and supports the zero-rated or reverse-charged treatment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP and DGDDI jointly exercise audit scrutiny over all export zero-rating and reverse-charge claims. Unfounded or fictitious export deductions are penalised under Article 1788 A CGI at 80% of the under-declared tax. Reckless or negligent zero-rating attracts the 40% penalty of Article 1728(b) CGI coupled with late-payment interest of 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI). Fraudulent conduct (fausse facturation, nonexistent exports, sham counterparties, forged bills of lading, circular trading) is prosecuted under Article 1741 CGI with criminal fines up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of five years, doubling for organised fraud, plus confiscation of instruments and proceeds. The VAT refund is retrospectively clawed back with statutory interest, and the unpaid tax remains indefinitely claimable in cases of concealed activity under Article L. 168 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales (10-year limitation for extraterritorial or artificial arrangements). For cross-border financial services, audit also tests whether the SARL maintained a French fixed establishment and whether the reverse-charge or zero-rate treatment artificially avoided VAT on effectively domestic supplies; any mischaracterisation triggers the same penalties, joint and several liability of the legal representative under Article 267 bis CGI, and publication of tax penalties. Persisting non-repatriation of export proceeds beyond the 180-day deadline also engages French exchange-control law and may lead to the transaction being recharacterised as a hidden distribution of profits subject to 30% withholding or corporation tax re-assessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, within the Eurosystem; foreign-exchange policy is primarily governed by the European Union and the European Central Bank. The French Treasury Directorate General, the French Customs authority, the Autorité des marchés financiers, and the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution exercise relevant reporting, market, payment, and prudential functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro, which is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no general French capital controls, prior approvals, surrender requirements, or restrictions on conversion of lawful commercial receipts, dividends, interest, or capital proceeds. Cross-border payments remain subject to sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering controls, beneficial-owner identification, payment-transparency requirements, tax compliance, and applicable EU financial-market rules. A regulated proprietary high-frequency trading business may require authorization as an investment firm or another applicable regulated status before commencing activities. Profit remittances should be supported by approved financial statements, corporate approvals, tax compliance evidence, and evidence that distributions do not breach French corporate-law capital-maintenance or solvency rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal statutory deadline requiring export receipts to be converted into euros. Export proceeds may normally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be received through correspondent-bank accounts, subject to accounting, tax, sanctions, customs, and anti-money-laundering controls. Commercial banks may require evidence of the underlying transaction, customs or invoice records, economic purpose, and source-of-funds information. Cash and certain equivalent payment instruments transported across EU external borders in amounts of EUR 10,000 or more are subject to applicable customs declaration requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. and relevant Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne network entity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ordinary operating payments and low to medium for a regulated proprietary high-frequency trading treasury. An EU electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide euro accounts, SEPA payments, cards, and selected foreign-currency services, but it is not a bank unless separately licensed. Client-money safeguarding, payment-purpose restrictions, transaction limits, safeguarding-bank dependencies, delayed compliance reviews, and inability to provide exchange-clearing, prime-brokerage, collateral, securities-settlement, or robust intraday liquidity services can make an EMI unsuitable as the primary treasury bank. Offshore digital EMIs without an EU passport, French branch, or acceptable EU regulatory status should not be used for core regulated activity. The company should maintain a regulated French or EU bank account and use an EMI only as a documented secondary rail after confirming licensing, safeguarding, sanctions, data, and counterparty arrangements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted following reliable electronic identification and verification of the company, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories, business activity, source of funds, and tax residence. Banks may nevertheless require an in-person meeting or video interview, notarized or apostilled documents, certified translations, a French operating address, or a local representative where ownership is non-resident, the activity is regulated, the structure is complex, or the proposed trading flows are high velocity. A regulated HFT applicant should expect enhanced management interviews and technical discussions concerning algorithms, venues, counterparties, controls, and capital provenance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear regulatory perimeter for proprietary algorithmic trading, market making, investment services, or direct exchange access
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written legal-perimeter memorandum; AMF or ACPR authorization, registration, or exemption analysis; copies of applications and approvals where applicable; activity matrix; venue and broker agreements; algorithmic-trading governance policy; pre-trade and post-trade control framework; market-abuse surveillance policy; and named compliance officer details.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency transaction volume inconsistent with the stated low-risk business classification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction-flow map; expected monthly volumes and values; venue list; currencies; average ticket size; peak intraday exposures; settlement timetable; counterparties; sample trade confirmations; expected incoming and outgoing payment narratives; and board-approved treasury policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership, layered holding companies, nominee arrangements, or difficulty identifying ultimate beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents for every ownership layer; current shareholder register; ultimate-beneficial-owner chart; passports and proof of address; corporate registry extracts; trust or foundation documents where relevant; ownership and control declarations; and evidence of commercial rationale for the structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of capital or funding from cryptocurrency, private investment vehicles, or unrelated third parties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements; bank statements; capital contribution agreements; investor identity and source-of-wealth evidence; tax returns or tax residence certificates where appropriate; sale or dividend documents; loan agreements; proof of originating-bank ownership; and a written funds-flow reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, or high-risk-jurisdiction exposure involving owners, directors, traders, brokers, or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions and PEP questionnaire; screening results; ownership and control analysis; documented risk assessment; enhanced due-diligence report; source-of-wealth evidence; counterparty approval records; and controls for blocked jurisdictions, restricted securities, and prohibited payment routes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, omnibus accounts, offshore accounts, or payment intermediaries inconsistent with the corporate profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Account-ownership schedule; broker and custodian agreements; permitted-account policy; reconciliation procedures; explanation of each intermediary; segregation-of-funds policy; and evidence that all settlement accounts are held in the company's name or with a properly documented regulated intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient substance in France or absence of credible management, technology, compliance, or operational infrastructure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or office evidence; employee and contractor records; organizational chart; technology architecture; disaster-recovery plan; outsourcing agreements; service-provider due diligence; employment and tax registrations; board minutes; and evidence of local decision-making and control functions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Algorithmic-trading risks, excessive messaging rates, market manipulation concerns, or weak kill-switch and surveillance controls
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Algorithm inventory; model approvals; change-management logs; testing results; kill-switch design; throttling and message-rate controls; conformance testing; incident logs; surveillance alerts; escalation procedures; business-continuity testing; and records demonstrating compliance with applicable MiFID II, delegated-regulation, venue, and market-abuse requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax transparency, VAT, corporate-tax, or beneficial-ownership reporting inconsistencies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax registration; tax residence certificate; corporate-tax filings; VAT position where relevant; CRS and FATCA self-certifications; beneficial-ownership filing evidence; transfer-pricing documentation; accounting records; and explanations for intercompany payments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inject capital from an account held in the investor's verified legal name to the SARL's French bank account, using a bank-to-bank SWIFT transfer or SEPA transfer where available. The payment narrative should identify the legal basis, such as paid-in share capital, share-premium contribution, shareholder loan, or qualifying contribution to equity. The bank should receive the subscription agreement, shareholder or board resolutions, capital-deposit certificate where applicable, updated articles or registry filing evidence, investor ownership documents, source-of-funds evidence, and tax-residence information. The receiving bank should verify the originating account, beneficial owner, purpose, sanctions status, and accounting treatment before release or use. Avoid third-party funding, unexplained pass-through accounts, cash, and crypto-originated funds unless the bank has approved enhanced due diligence. For a regulated trading entity, segregate regulatory capital, operating cash, margin collateral, and client or third-party funds, and reconcile each category daily.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or TARGET services for euro payments, and SWIFT cross-border payments for non-euro currencies or jurisdictions outside the SEPA area. SWIFT MT103 is a bank messaging format rather than an independent settlement system; payment instructions must contain complete originator, beneficiary, address, purpose, invoice or contract reference, and intermediary-bank data. Use commercial letters of credit, documentary collections, or bank guarantees only for genuine goods or service transactions and not to disguise trading, capital, or investment flows. For securities and derivatives, use the regulated broker, exchange, clearing member, central counterparty, custodian, or settlement agent designated in the relevant agreement. Fedwire is a United States dollar domestic settlement rail and is not a French domestic rail; it may be used only through an eligible US correspondent or broker for USD settlement. Maintain payment approval matrices, dual authorization, sanctions screening, invoice or contract support, beneficiary verification, daily bank reconciliation, and exception reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for documented operating, settlement, or balance-sheet exposures, subject to bank counterparty limits, confirmations, valuation, collateral terms, and applicable EMIR reporting and risk-mitigation requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards where the reference currency or market convention requires cash settlement, provided the instrument is executed with an appropriately regulated counterparty and is supported by a documented underlying exposure or approved risk-management mandate.

Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity, funding, and currency transformation, subject to counterparty credit limits, maturity controls, collateral arrangements, valuation, and EMIR obligations.

Currency options, collars, and option combinations for hedging identifiable exposures, subject to product-governance, appropriateness or suitability requirements, premium and liquidity controls, accounting treatment, and prohibition of speculative structures outside the approved treasury mandate.

Cross-currency swaps for longer-term funding or structural currency exposure, subject to board-approved limits, collateral and close-out provisions, independent valuation, EMIR reporting, and stress testing.

Hedging documentation should identify the exposure, hedge ratio, tenor, authorized counterparties, execution venue, valuation source, collateral terms, accounting designation, termination rights, and prohibited speculative uses. MiFID II, EMIR, market-abuse, sanctions, accounting, and prudential requirements may apply depending on the entity's authorization, counterparties, and instrument classification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale) comprising Form 2065-SD and schedules 2050–2057, with statement of profit distribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via certified electronic filing (EDI/TDFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year taxpayers: second business day after 1 May (usually 2–4 May); off-calendar-year taxpayers: within 3 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges under Article 1728 CGI: 10% if filed after deadline but within 30 days of formal notice, 20% if filed within 30 days of formal notice, 40% if not filed within that period, and 80% for concealed activity; monthly late interest at 0.20% (Article 1727 CGI); enforced by tax lien and garnishment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of certified annual accounts (bilan, compte de résultat, annexe) with the Commercial Register (RCS formalities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Guichet Unique operated by INPI, transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for registration at the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting must approve accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end; deposit must occur within 1 month of approval and in all cases by 7 months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year: 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to €7,500 for a legal entity (€1,500 for natural persons); possible court-ordered injunction with astreinte; persistent non-filing enables the Registrar to initiate administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary shareholders' meeting (AGO) approving annual accounts, granting discharge to the gérant, and allocating profit or loss
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records only (minutes recorded in the register of decisions); no separate public filing beyond the accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end (calendar-year: by 30 June); minutes must be recorded and signed in the corporate register immediately after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: On default, any partner may petition the President of the Tribunal de Commerce to convene the meeting or appoint a mandataire ad hoc at the gérant's cost; the gérant may be held personally liable for resulting late-filing penalties and consequential damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) annual declaration and final instalment of the local business tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP — Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration (Form 1447-C) filed with the annual 2065-SD package; advance instalment of 50% due by 15 June and final balance due by 15 December of the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% automatic increase plus 0.20% monthly overdue interest; absence of declaration allows tax ex-officio assessment with penalty up to 40%, enforced by bank lien.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner declaration (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) and ongoing accuracy maintenance of RCS identity data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Guichet Unique (INPI) / RCS kept by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No standalone annual return is due if nothing has changed; any change in beneficial ownership or registered RCS details must be filed within 30 days of the event; status is re-verified at each annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted beneficial-owner filing: imprisonment up to 6 months and fine up to €7,500 for natural persons, €37,500 for legal persons; repeated omissions may trigger RCS administrative strike-off.

stage_6.entry_description: Net fiscal profit for the year after the statement of the ordinary trading result and capital gains; basis for IS at 25%
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent consolidation under parent-subsidiary regime requires upload of form 2058-A with the domestic trading result; no relief for a DTA at profit level
